devcon.name: DevCon
devcon.about: Talks from DevCon Seattle. Tickets at http://ticketmaster.com/event/devcon-2026

offgrid-routes.name: Off-Grid Routes
offgrid-routes.about: Tomas Reyes walks, trains and ferries across places the guidebooks skip. No sponsors on the trail, a lot of tea. Route notes in every description.

lena-covers.name: Lena Vasquez Covers
lena-covers.about: Piano and voice covers, one take, recorded in a rented room above a bakery. New cover every other Sunday. Full versions on http://spotify.com/ and http://music.youtube.com/

pixelfoundry.name: Pixel Foundry
pixelfoundry.about: Indie game deep dives, speedrun breakdowns and the occasional twelve-hour build stream. Hosted by Jules Park and Dmitri Kessler.

ironclad.name: Ironclad Fitness
ironclad.about: Coach Nadia Brooks. Strength training for people with a job, a knee, and twenty minutes. No supplements, no before-and-after shots.

wirecut.name: Wirecut News
wirecut.about: Two-minute clips of the stories that matter, cut from the day's wires. Sources linked. Corrections pinned. Longer reads at http://reuters.com/ and http://arstechnica.com/

sawdust.name: Sawdust Society
sawdust.about: Woodworking from a two-car garage in Duluth. Hand tools first, power tools when honest. Plans sold at http://etsy.com/ — Ray Lindqvist.

latenight-loop.name: Late Night Loop
latenight-loop.about: Clips from Late Night Loop with Hugo Bramble, taped nightly in Studio 4B. Monologues, desk bits and guests who did not expect the follow-up question.

tonguetied.name: Tongue Tied
tonguetied.about: Learn Spanish and Japanese from Sofia Ruiz and Kenji Tanaka, who are learning each other's language on camera and making every mistake so you do not have to.

determinism-intro.title: What deterministic simulation actually means
determinism-intro.description: Same seed, same inputs, same bytes out. Fifteen minutes on the three things you have to give up to get there: the wall clock, ambient randomness, and unordered iteration. Background reading: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deterministic_simulation

flaky-test-windows.title: Debugging a test that only fails on Windows

devcon-keynote.title: DevCon Seattle 2026 keynote — the reproducibility track
devcon-keynote.description: The opening keynote, plus the full schedule for the reproducibility track. Tickets: http://ticketmaster.com/event/devcon-2026

one-pan-chicken-thighs.title: One pan, six chicken thighs, nobody does the dishes
one-pan-chicken-thighs.description: Crispy skin-side down, then the onions go in the same fat and finish under the lid. Fifteen minutes hands-on, thirty total. Serves four, or two people who had a day. Written recipe at the end of the video.

comments.author: mina_ok
comments.text: Thighs, never breasts. I will die on this hill.

knife-skills-ten-minutes.title: Every knife cut you actually use, in ten minutes
knife-skills-ten-minutes.description: Rock chop, claw grip, the bias cut, and why your onion cries less when the knife is sharp. Sharpening at 7:10. No mandolines were harmed.

weeknight-ramen.title: Weeknight ramen from a store-bought broth that tastes like it wasn't
weeknight-ramen.description: Doctor the carton: ginger, a spoon of miso, the soy-butter thing. Jammy egg at 6:40. Related: http://youtube.com/watch?v=knife-skills-ten-minutes for the scallion cut.

comments.author: ktanaka
comments.text: As a Japanese person: this is fine, and the miso is correct.

sheet-pan-salmon.title: Sheet pan salmon and the vegetables you were going to throw away
sheet-pan-salmon.description: Broccoli stems, the sad half of a lemon, the last of the potatoes. Everything at 220C for eighteen minutes, salmon goes in for the last nine. Sunday meal prep without the meal-prep face.

faroe-by-bus.title: Crossing the Faroe Islands by public bus in four days
faroe-by-bus.description: Eighteen islands, one bus pass, a sub-sea tunnel that plays music, and a ferry that runs when the captain feels like it. Route notes and the bus timetable I used are in the pinned comment. Background: http://en.wikipedia.org/

comments.author: tomasr
comments.text: Timetable: Route 300 to Klaksvik, then 500 and the 58 ferry. Check the weather board first.

night-train-lisbon.title: The overnight train from Hendaye to Lisbon, second class
night-train-lisbon.description: A twelve hour sleeper with a shared corridor, a dining car that closes at nine, and the best sunrise I have filmed. Booking tips at 21:00. No sponsor on this one.

comments.author: sofia_r
comments.text: Lisbon at dawn from a train window. You got it.

kyrgyz-yurt-week.title: A week in a Kyrgyz yurt with no signal and a horse named Bek
kyrgyz-yurt-week.description: Song-Kol lake at 3000 metres, fermented mare's milk, and a family who let me help with the sheep. Filmed on a single battery. Route from Kochkor at 24:10.

comments.author: tomasr
comments.text: Boiled, always. Iodine tablets as backup. Covered at 17:00.

cover-rainy-window.title: Rainy Window (piano and voice, one take)
cover-rainy-window.description: One take, one microphone, the bakery downstairs pulling the morning trays out at 2:14 if you listen closely. Full version on http://spotify.com/

comments.author: dmitri_k
comments.text: The bridge at 1:50 is the best part of the original and you made it better.

cover-northbound.title: Northbound (acoustic cover) — requested 400 times
cover-northbound.description: You asked, repeatedly. Capo on the third fret, dropped D, the harmony is me twice. Chords in the pinned comment. Streaming at http://music.youtube.com/

cover-summer-static.title: Summer Static (live at the rooftop show)
cover-summer-static.description: Recorded on the roof of the bakery for thirty people and a heat wave. The piano was out of tune by the second chorus and I kept it. Setlist at the end.

why-ice-is-slippery.title: Why ice is slippery (the textbook answer is wrong)
why-ice-is-slippery.description: Pressure melting cannot explain a skate. Friction melting cannot explain a puck sitting still. The real answer involves a liquid-like layer that exists at minus thirty. Sources on screen and at http://en.wikipedia.org/

how-gps-corrects-time.title: GPS satellites run their clocks slow on purpose
how-gps-corrects-time.description: Special relativity slows them, general relativity speeds them, and the net is 38 microseconds a day, which would put you ten kilometres off by tomorrow. The engineers pre-corrected the clocks before launch. The clean explanation starts at 3:05.

comments.author: dmitri_k
comments.text: Ten kilometres a day is a really good number for a headline.

determinism-in-nature.title: Is anything in nature actually deterministic?
determinism-in-nature.description: Three-body chaos, a double pendulum, and one line of quantum mechanics. A companion piece to a very different kind of video: http://youtube.com/watch?v=determinism-intro

why-bread-rises.title: Why bread rises, from the yeast's point of view
why-bread-rises.description: Gas, gluten, and a foam that sets. Includes a microscope, a proofing box and Mina from Pan Fried, who brought the dough: http://youtube.com/channel/panfried

comments.author: mina_ok
comments.text: I brought the dough and stayed for the microscope.

hollow-depths-any-percent.title: Hollow Depths any% in 41:12 — the run, explained
hollow-depths-any-percent.description: A new world record and the four skips that made it. The wall clip at 12:40 was found by a viewer in chat. Full VOD with commentary; timestamps in the description.

comments.author: dmitri_k
comments.text: The 12:40 clip is still not fully understood and I love that.

indie-dev-twelve-hour-build.title: We built a game in twelve hours, live (stream VOD)
indie-dev-twelve-hour-build.description: Jules draws, Dmitri codes, chat names everything. The result is a fishing game where the fish judge you. Build starts at 4:00, the panic at 9:12:00. Source at http://github.com/

pixel-art-101.title: Pixel art 101: the four rules that make sprites read at 16x16
pixel-art-101.description: Silhouette, palette limits, cluster shapes, and where to cheat on outlines. Twenty minutes with a live sprite, from blob to knight.

twenty-minute-strength.title: Twenty-minute full body strength with one kettlebell
twenty-minute-strength.description: Six moves, three rounds, one bell, no jumping. Knee-friendly swaps at 3:15. This is the workout I do when I have a meeting in twenty-five minutes.

desk-posture-fix.title: Fix your desk posture in four stretches (no equipment)
desk-posture-fix.description: Hip flexors, thoracic spine, neck, wrists. Five minutes, done at your desk, filmed at my desk. Do it at 2pm when the slump happens.

running-first-5k.title: Your first 5K: an eight-week plan for people who hate running
running-first-5k.description: Walk-run intervals, the shoe talk you did not ask for, and why week five is where everyone quits. Plan printable in the pinned comment.

wirecut-chip-export-rules.title: New chip export rules take effect: what changes in two minutes
wirecut-chip-export-rules.description: The updated export control list, who is affected, and the three dates that matter. Full text and the agency statement at http://reuters.com/ and http://arstechnica.com/

wirecut-heat-grid.title: Heat wave and the grid: why your power flickered this week
wirecut-heat-grid.description: Demand peaks, the reserve margin, and the one substation that was the actual problem. Sources at http://reuters.com/

hand-cut-dovetails.title: Hand-cut dovetails for the first time, honestly
hand-cut-dovetails.description: Every gap, every mistake, one chisel that was too dull until minute nine. By the end they fit. Plans and the marking gauge I use at http://etsy.com/

comments.author: ray_l
comments.text: Sharpen first. I say it every video and I still didn't.

workbench-weekend.title: A proper workbench in one weekend from construction lumber
workbench-weekend.description: Laminate, flatten, one vise, done Sunday night. Cut list on screen at 2:00. Total cost under two hundred, because the lumber yard was kind.

wood-finish-comparison.title: Six wood finishes, one board, six months later
wood-finish-comparison.description: Oil, wax, shellac, water-based poly, oil-based poly and nothing. Water rings, sun fade, a dropped mug. The winner surprised me.

loop-monologue-robot-vacuum.title: Hugo's robot vacuum has been sending him emails (monologue)
loop-monologue-robot-vacuum.description: The vacuum has feelings, the fridge is jealous, and the week's headlines get the same treatment. Taped Tuesday in Studio 4B.

comments.author: hugo_b
comments.text: The vacuum has since been given a raise.

loop-desk-bit-deterministic.title: Hugo tries to explain deterministic simulation to his mother (desk bit)

spanish-in-30-days-week1.title: Spanish in 30 days, week one: the 200 words that carry a conversation
spanish-in-30-days-week1.description: Sofia teaches, Kenji learns, both of them get corrected by Sofia's grandmother. Word list in the pinned comment. Free, no app.

comments.author: ktanaka
comments.text: I am still being corrected. Week one was six months ago.

japanese-counters-explained.title: Japanese counters, finally explained by someone who suffered
japanese-counters-explained.description: Hon, mai, hiki, tsu. Kenji explains, Sofia counts pencils wrong for four minutes, everyone learns. Sheet in the pinned comment.

swap-day-immersion.title: Swap day: Sofia speaks only Japanese, Kenji only Spanish, for 24 hours
swap-day-immersion.description: A grocery store, a train station, a phone call with grandma. Subtitled in both languages. The panic at the pharmacy is at 9:30.
